newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: CambodiaN film festival opens without top guest.
newsitem.headline: CambodiaN film festival opens without top guest.

text.p: A landmark film festival got under way in Cambodia on Saturday, but guest of honour Alain Delon failed to make it for the opening.
The First Southeast Asian Biennial Film Festival kicked off with the showing of Cemeng 2005, the Last Primadonna.

Alain Delon was due to attend an open-air showing of his 1981 film--For the Skin of a Cop (Pour la Peau d'Un Flic), but organisers said his arrival had been postponed and they hoped he would be able to make it on Sunday.
Twelve films from Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam will be taking part in competition during the week-long festival.
Indonesian actress, Christine Hakim, heads an eight-member international jury for the competition.
Movies from Cambodia, Burma, China, India, Iran and France, including a retrospective of Delon films, will also be shown in a fringe event.

The festival, which is expected to become a regular event based in Phnom Penh, has been organised and sponsored by the French Embassy, the missions of Southeast Asian countries, the Ministry of Culture and private companies.

"I can feel today in this room, spirit for the future, for us to work together," Hakim said in a press conference also attended by international guests, including acclaimed French actresses Anne Parillaud and Valerie Kaprisky.
